data.name: UI primitive
data.Definition: A small wrapper in the dashboard design system layer around one interface element, such as a button, input, dialog or table, that fixes its look so screens compose it instead of styling from scratch.

data.name: Slot attribute
data.Definition: The data-slot attribute every primitive puts on its element, naming the part (for example button or dialog-content) so parents and tests can target it.

data.name: Chart config
data.Definition: The ChartConfig map from a series key to a label, an optional icon and either one colour or a light and dark colour pair, shared by a chart container and its tooltip and legend.

data.name: Caller class names override primitive defaults
data.Statement: Every primitive merges its default Tailwind classes with the caller className through cn, so a caller override replaces a conflicting default instead of stacking with it.

data.name: Toggle group settings win over item settings
data.Statement: A toggle group passes its variant, size and spacing to its items through a context, and an item uses its own variant or size only when the group sets none.

data.name: Chart parts require a chart container
data.Statement: The chart tooltip and legend content read the chart config through a context, and using them outside a chart container throws an error.

refs.quote: throw new Error("useChart must be used within a <ChartContainer />")

data.name: Sheet opens from the right by default
data.Statement: A sheet slides in from the right unless a side of top, bottom or left is given, and both sheet and dialog show a close button unless showCloseButton is false.

data.name: Tooltip provider default delay is zero
data.Statement: The tooltip provider shows tooltips without a hover delay unless the app gives a delayDuration, and the dashboard roots give 200 milliseconds.

data.name: Chart colours follow the light and dark theme
data.Statement: A chart writes one set of colour variables for the light theme and one scoped to the dark selector, so series colours change with the theme.

refs.quote: const THEMES = { light: "", dark: ".dark" } as const

data.Mitigation: Cover primitives through the screens that use them, or add tests beside the primitives.
data.name: Primitives have no tests of their own
data.Risk: No test file lives in this folder, so a change to a shared primitive is exercised only through the screens that import it.

data.name: Which primitives are unused
data.Question: Dialog, Alert, Accordion and Progress are imported only by the component gallery. Should they stay in the layer or be removed?
